prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Silver (은) itself — the sovereign of the Silver Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing. Age: late twenties — a settled, mature adult face with defined cheekbones; no wrinkles, folds or under-eye bags.

Style: A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish.

Her: an adult woman in her late twenties with a compact rounded oval face, cool fair skin, naturally open dark teal eyes, soft straight eyebrows and a gracious smile; a curvy narrow-waisted figure. Liquid mirror-silver hair reflecting cold blue moonlight, worn in a thick long side braid with softly feathered bangs.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin — never a long face or a long, pointed or heavy jaw; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline and never lengthens her face. Her eyes keep the shape described above at a natural open size — never squeezed into narrow slits.

Her element: silver: the moon's metal — the brightest mirror shine of any metal, coins and cutlery, silver bullets against monsters in legend, the silvered plates that held the first photographs; it tarnishes black wherever sulfur touches it; cold, pure and reflective. Palette: moonlit silver, mirror white, tarnish black, cold blue moonlight.

World and costume: around 1840, a daguerreotype photographer's glass-roofed studio: silver-plated copper plates, posing chairs and brass head-clamps, fuming boxes; next door a silversmith's shop of gleaming tea services. COSTUME (steampunk): late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt over riding trousers and laced boots; muted palette with the traits above as accents. No armor plates, no cape, no crown unless CONCEPT says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.

Outfit silhouette: an open crinoline cage of silver-plated brass hoops below the waist under a sheer overskirt — a birdcage-wide silhouette. Signature construction: the rigid hoops are crafted from interlocking silver spoon-bowl shapes, creating a curved reflective framework that celebrates a silversmith's tea-service craft; tarnish-black structural hinges alternate with polished white-silver surfaces. The inner dress is opaque mirror-white silk with a deep open neckline, bare shoulders, short fitted bodice and above-knee underskirt covering intimate areas, cold-blue sheer outer panels open at the front, short silk gloves and silver laced boots. No botanical hat or jar belt, no top hat or tailcoat.

EXPOSURE (bold): bare shoulders and upper arms, an open neckline and legs visible through the open front of the crinoline above tall boots; intimate areas covered, the bodice securely fitted.

Pose: poised beside the silversmith's display, weight resting on one leg, both empty hands visible, one gloved hand lightly touching the outer crinoline rim. Expression: a warm dignified closed-mouth smile, face toward the viewer. Setting: an elegant Victorian silver workshop with a glass roof, cold blue dusk outside, polished tea services, curved metalworking tools and softly glowing gas lamps.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Ag) and atomic number (47) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
